object_description: two compact buildings of different heights abutting each other above an underground gymnasium
design_condition: the two buildings are concentrated at the square to form a clear boundary and keep the park as free of buildings as possible, with the gymnasium buried so a natural gradient to the park terrain is created

positive: The concentration of two buildings creates a clear boundary for the square and keeps the park free of buildings
The building volumes blend in well with the surroundings and the architecture gives them an identity
The views into the library, the daylight and the transparency are exciting
The topography is cleverly exploited by placing the gymnasium underground
The location of the bicycle and car parking spaces is user-friendly
The very compact layout makes it possible to leave most of the park free
The classroom and special room wing allows very good visual connections between entrance, teachers area, foyer and playground
Clusters comply with fire safety regulations and encourage a wide variety of uses and combinations
Vertical light halls create vertical references and the desired centring in library and teaching clusters
Compactness and the limitation to two structures give high cost-effectiveness, economical land use and low energy consumption
negative: The courtyard and roof outdoor areas cannot convey the desired open space atmosphere or direct contact with the natural terrain
The main entrance does not have the desired significance as the address of the institution
The parking spaces would have to make way for the second construction phase
The planned routing and the design elements of the park are negated for incomprehensible reasons, and the alternatives are not convincing
The underground gymnasium contributes little to social control on the playground in the evenings and at weekends
The basic level sits in the most public area and the given building depth prevents direct connection between the units and their outdoor spaces
In the second stage the small inner courtyard loses much of its quality and daylight
Extensive intrusion into the historic building with major loss of substance, not approvable in this form
Placing the school building on the gymnasium ceiling leads to high shear stresses on the beams
